# PREFIX-790 / R6 — Exact cut-interface compatibility, ghost-path accounting, and observer-typed minimal residual states

Date: 2026-11-15 (Asia/Shanghai).
Status: AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_INTEGER_REGRESSION / UNREVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED.
Research context: independent external integer-path observer continuation after PREFIX-789. Historical researcher EM-DIRECT-E77192; recorded Activity RA-66BBE259AEE1AD543D9454A3; original own SID MCP-d9aca4ec6e00440eba66035326ea5a4e. No shared X6 claim or result is asserted.
Frozen science: awdawmip/enterprise-math@f42f2906d77f24085c123f3ccfe9667d41caa96d.
Predecessor: research_notes/portable_direct/2026-11-15_r6_prefix789_provenance_preserving_modular_path_transfer.md.

## Question and finite typed interface

PREFIX-789 established that independently attainable modular residues may belong to different complete paths. Here we determine how much junction/source information is necessary to compose prefixes with suffixes and which observer-specific quotients can be exact.

Choose a finite set K of labelled cut states. Each permitted complete route is represented exactly once by a prefix p in L_v and a suffix r in R_v at the same v in K. The L_v and R_v are finite multisets of **path identities**, so equal weights do not erase multiplicity. The Boolean guard C_v(p,r) says whether the pair is permitted. Every permitted path has integer additive weight a(p)+b(r); assume at least one permitted path. A visible state v need not make all prefix/suffix combinations legal: hidden source, signed-Port, or earlier event-time information may enter C_v.

Work in the nonnegative Laurent polynomial semiring S=N[X,X^{-1}]. Define

    H = sum_{v in K} sum_{p in L_v} sum_{r in R_v} C_v(p,r) X^(a(p)+b(r)),
    L_v(X) = sum_{p in L_v} X^a(p),
    R_v(X) = sum_{r in R_v} X^b(r).

Let H_state = sum_v L_v R_v and H_free = (sum_v L_v)(sum_v R_v). Reduction pi_m:S -> N[Z/mZ], m>=1, reduces exponents modulo m but retains nonnegative integer coefficients exactly. It is the restricted counting observer of PREFIX-789, not an automatically valid native X6 observer.

## Theorem 790.1 — Exact decomposition of fabricated paths

The coefficientwise nonnegative identities

    H_free = H + G_cross + G_guard,
    G_cross = sum_{v != w} L_v R_w,
    G_guard = sum_v sum_{p in L_v,r in R_v:C_v(p,r)=0} X^(a(p)+b(r))

hold in S and in every modulo-m semiring after applying pi_m. Consequently:

* H_state=H as an exact counting polynomial if and only if every within-state prefix/suffix identity pair is compatible.
* H_free=H as an exact counting polynomial if and only if both ghost expressions vanish.
* For a fixed target residue t modulo m, the excess count manufactured by free composition equals [t]pi_m(G_cross+G_guard). The target count is exact iff this coefficient is zero.

Proof. Expand the free product over all ordered prefix/suffix identities. Every pair belongs uniquely to one of three disjoint classes: different cut states; the same cut state but forbidden by C_v; the same state and permitted by C_v. By the unique-decomposition hypothesis, the last class is in bijection with actual complete paths. The others are the two displayed ghost terms. All coefficients are nonnegative, so equality of full counting polynomials forces the absence of all forbidden pairs. The modular homomorphism preserves addition and these multiplicities. QED.

Counting equality is stronger than reachable-support equality: a ghost may increase the count at an already-reachable residue without adding a new supported residue.

## Theorem 790.2 — Exact minimal typed continuation state

For each state v and prefix p define the suffix-identity continuation row

    alpha_v(p) = (C_v(p,r))_{r in R_v} in {0,1}^{|R_v|}.

Let A_v be the distinct rows, and let

    L_(v,alpha) = sum_{p:alpha_v(p)=alpha} X^a(p),
    R_(v,alpha) = sum_{r:alpha(r)=1} X^b(r).

Then

    H = sum_{v in K} sum_{alpha in A_v} L_(v,alpha) R_(v,alpha).       (790.2)

Moreover, within a fixed v, partitioning prefix identities by their rows is the coarsest deterministic state quotient that preserves every possible suffix-identity membership predicate. Include an empty continuation row when the ability to detect dead prefixes is observed.

Proof. Expand (790.2): every permitted pair occurs in exactly the summand of its prefix's row and contributes its weight once. If two rows differ, there is a named suffix r accepted after one prefix and forbidden after the other. Any deterministic state that merges them would return the same answer to the suffix-membership query, which is incorrect. Equal rows answer all such queries equally, proving sufficiency and coarseness under this declared typed observer. QED.

This theorem supplies a finite-state repair for a hidden-history compatibility guard. It introduces a *state memory distinction*, not an additional native spatial axis.

## Theorem 790.3 — Count-observer and modular coarsening

For the exact integer-sum **count** observer, associate each prefix p with the weighted continuation polynomial

    Q_v(p)=sum_{r:C_v(p,r)=1} X^b(r).

Group prefixes having identical Q_v(p), and for a group B with common Q_B replace its contribution by

    (sum_{p in B}X^a(p)) Q_B.

The replacement exactly preserves H. It is the coarsest quotient of the form "one common suffix polynomial per group" uniformly correct for **every independent assignment of prefix-count inputs**. For a fixed modular-count observer, the corresponding quotient groups by equality of pi_m(Q_v(p)). For pure modular reachability, grouping by equality of supported suffix residues suffices in the Boolean support semiring.

Proof. Distributivity gives the sufficiency of each grouping. For uniform necessity, set every independent prefix input but one to zero and set the remaining input to 1. Exactness then requires that the group's common suffix factor equal the selected prefix's Q_v(p). Therefore every two prefixes grouped together must have equal continuation polynomials. Applying pi_m and then the support homomorphism gives the stated observer-specific relaxations. QED.

Thus the available quotient hierarchy is

    named/typed suffix-identity row
       -> exact integer-weight continuation count
       -> modulo-m continuation count
       -> modulo-m continuation support.

Each arrow may merge states but grants preservation only for that observer and its declared future-operation scope. Particular fixed prefix populations may admit accidental extra coincidences; the preceding coarseness is prefix-uniform. When future operations inspect path order, branch/source identities, event time, Port guards or other moduli, those dimensions must be retained or separately certified.

## Exact counterexamples and constructions

A. **Erasing a junction state creates a target.** There are two cut states, alpha and beta. At alpha, the single prefix and suffix both have weight 0; at beta, both have weight 1. Same-state pairs are all legal:

    H = 1+X^2,
    H_free = (1+X)^2 = 1+2X+X^2.

At target T=1, modulo 3, the true residue count is 0 while free composition claims two witnesses. The actual integer target distance is 1; the collapsed distance is 0.

B. **Keeping a visible state can still invent paths.** There is one visible state with prefixes p0,p1 of weights 0,1 and suffixes r0,r1 of weights 0,1. Only (p0,r0) and (p1,r1) may compose. The two compatibility rows are (1,0) and (0,1). The true H is 1+X^2, while L_vR_v is 1+2X+X^2. Recording the row/one-bit distinction restores the exact transfer.

C. **Typed distinctions may disappear for a declared count observer.** If two suffix identities both have weight 0, the typed rows (1,0) and (0,1) are distinct yet both continuation polynomials equal 1. For the exact scalar-weight histogram, these rows can be merged; suffix-identity questions still require both. In a different example, suffix sets with weights {0} and {0,0} have identical supports but different multiplicities. Replacing both by the same representative keeps target support but loses full count (3 real paths versus 2 in the replacement).

## Exact algorithm and reproducibility

Given explicit finite prefix/suffix identities and compatibility guards, computing the typed continuation rows uses O(sum_v |L_v| |R_v|) Boolean guard inspections. Histogram multiplication can then implement (790.2), with arbitrary exact integer coefficients and Laurent exponents. A fixed modulus uses m residue bins; a bounded exact-integer-weight range permits dense arrays, while sparse supports permit integer dictionaries. Explicit histories and guards may be exponentially numerous relative to a succinct source graph, consistent with PREFIX-788's restricted NP-completeness finding.

Companion reproducible source: research_notes/portable_direct/PREFIX790_R6_CUT_INTERFACE_CERTIFICATE_CHECK.py.
Result JSON: research_notes/portable_direct/PREFIX790_R6_CUT_INTERFACE_CERTIFICATE_RESULTS.json.

The locally executed standard-library Python checker used deterministic seed 79020261115 with exact Counter/integer arithmetic. Its final version returned ALL_CHECKS_PASS PREFIX790 CUT_INTERFACE_MINIMAL_RESIDUAL with 278534 counted exact assertions. Coverage: 4096 two-step parallel-edge cut graphs, 28672 modular cut comparisons, 4096 Boolean compatibility interfaces and 28672 modular compatibility comparisons; moduli (2,3,5,6,7,11,13), finite sampled integer edge weights. On generated guard interfaces, exact-weight suffix grouping strictly reduced typed row classes 171 times; modular grouping did so 4445 times. There were 16748 ghost-only residue appearances across modular cut cases. These are regression facts. The universal equalities and coarseness assertions are established by the above combinatorial proofs.

## Scientific frontier and recovery

1. Read genuine native BRC/X6 Cell, Link, Port, branch, signed-source, event time and transition-guard records under their actual frozen source pin. Identify whether a visible native cut state gives universal prefix/suffix composability, or obtain a concrete history-dependent guard witness.
2. For a declared finite native horizon, build continuation rows retaining the exact typed future-operation predicates. If a historical relation restricts suffixes, refine the state before evaluating integer-residue transfers.
3. Evaluate a quotient only against its actual observer (typed continuation / exact weighted count / modular count / support) and the required future operations. No native comparison grid exclusions are added by this external graph theorem.

Scientific status: author proof and seeded exact regression; independent review and project admission pending.
